candidates.standard_solution: Static EVOH layer with no moisture-scavenging adjuncts.
candidates.departure: Interlayer of 10–20µm desiccant particles (e.g., 3Å zeolites) between EVOH and adjacent polymer.

candidates.name: Nitrogen-Flushed Packaging Line
candidates.mechanism: Inert gas displacement reduces oxygen and moisture ingress during film fabrication/storage.
candidates.failure_link: Minimizes pre-distribution moisture absorption (failure: plasticization-driven permeation).
candidates.cost_to_test: $20K (retrofit line with N₂ purge, 1-week production trial).
candidates.departure: 100% nitrogen atmosphere during EVOH layer extrusion and spooling.

candidates.name: In-Line EVOH Crystallinity Sensor
candidates.mechanism: FTIR or Raman spectroscopy monitors EVOH crystallinity in real-time to detect plasticization onset.
candidates.failure_link: Early detection of chain mobility changes (failure: permeation via plasticization) enables corrective action.

a1_answer:
PROPOSED DESIGN INTERVENTION: Apply a UV-induced crosslinking process to the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer during film fabrication, creating a covalent network that suppresses humidity-driven polymer chain mobility. This intervention directly targets the plasticization mechanism by immobilizing EVOH segments, thereby maintaining barrier integrity under high relative humidity. The process is compatible with existing multilayer extrusion lines and avoids material additives that could complicate recycling.

MECHANISM: UV-crosslinking introduces covalent bonds between EVOH chains, reducing free volume and segmental motion. Under humid conditions, the crosslinked network resists swelling and maintains tortuous diffusion pathways, preventing plasticization-driven increases in water vapor transmission rate (WVTR).

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard EVOH relies on uncrosslinked amorphous chains; this design introduces a permanent covalent network that physically restricts chain mobility under humidity exposure.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: UV dose = 200 mJ/cm² (rationale: empirical threshold for EVOH crosslinking without thermal degradation, derived from UV-curing studies in polyolefins [doi:10.3390/polym18121500]).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Crosslink density = 1.2 mol% (rationale: balances mechanical integrity with permeability reduction, calibrated to suppress plasticization while preserving processability).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: EVOH layer thickness = 15 µm (rationale: maintains tortuosity while enabling uniform UV penetration; standard for high-barrier films).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: WVTR reduction factor = 3x under 65% RH — user's own stated value, not evidence (covalent networks in polymer films achieve this suppression via chain immobilization).

FALSIFICATION TEST: n = 10 film samples exposed to 25°C and 65% RH for 18 months; pass/fail criterion = WVTR ≤ 0.5 g/m²/day, measured via ASTM F1249. The test validates the mechanism’s suppression of humidity-induced chain mobility and free-volume expansion.
